hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=x^3-x^2-x$ and $g(x)=-2$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and every point where they intersect represents a solution of $f(x)=g(x)$.

options.alt: A cubic function graph and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph moves from negative infinity and increases from left to right to a point around (negative one fourth, one fourth), then decreases to (one, negative one). It increases to the point (two, two) and continues to positive infinity. The horizontal line is at y equals negative two and intersects the cubic function graph at one point.

hints.content:
The graphs intersect once, so the equation has *one solution*.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation: A cubic graph changes between increasing and decreasing at no more than 2 points. Since we see both those points in the graph, we know the values of the function to the left of the point will all be less than $y=-2$ and the values to the right of the point will all be greater than $y=-2$. So there are no more intersection points.
options.showPrompt: How do we know that there aren't any other solutions?
